templates: Worth separating two things here. Most of the time this is not the formula. It is how warm the product sat in storage before it ever shipped. We run a 240,000 sq ft temperature controlled warehouse outside {city} and hold inventory at a steady temperature the whole time it waits.

The damage usually happens while it waits, not on the way out. If inventory sits warm for a month, potency and texture go with it. We keep it temperature controlled the whole time, FDA registered, {city} area.
Quick reframe. Storage time plus heat is what causes rancidity and separation. We hold inventory temperature controlled from receiving all the way to pick, outside {city}.
